# What's new in Nucleo


### A brief overview of recent company and product updates from the Nucleo team.


[Angelica Iacovelli](https://substack.com/@angelicaiacovelli)


,[Luca Pegolotti](https://substack.com/@lucapegolotti)


, and[Tisha Mazumdar](https://substack.com/@tishamazumdarnucleo)


Oct 28, 2026


Two updates from the past few weeks: an award at MICCAI for our pan-cancer lesion model, and an abstract accepted at RSNA 2026, where we are also hosting a dinner.


## Nucleo wins Best Pan-cancer Segmentation Accuracy at MICCAI


We built the state of the art for whole-body tumor detection and segmentation. Our pan-cancer model just won


**Best Pan-cancer Segmentation Accuracy** at


**FLARE 2026** at MICCAI, #1 medical imaging conference in the world, for the paper “Pan-cancer Lesion Segmentation in CT under Heterogeneous and Partial Annotation”.


Most oncologic imaging models are trained on one tumor type in one organ. Ours segments every lesion, across organ systems, from a single CT.


> *Best Pan-cancer Segmentation Accuracy, FLARE 2026 at MICCAI.*


**Challenge 1: scale.** Lesion volumes span four orders of magnitude, from sub-millilitre nodules to litre-scale masses. 52% of annotated lesions in the training corpus are below 1 mL. Volume-weighted losses underweight small lesions; count-weighted losses are dominated by them.


**Challenge 2: label semantics.** Training data pools 28 public cohorts (~17k CT scans) annotated under different protocols. Most label only the target lesion. A voxel marked “background” may be an unannotated lesion, which turns into incorrect negative supervision.


Architecture mattered less than expected. Swin transformer encoders, mixture-of-experts routing and distillation from a CT foundation model did not outperform a well-tuned residual 3D U-Net. Most of the gains came from data, sampling and evaluation choices.


Results: 81.2% DSC and 76.4% NSD on the hidden validation set, at ~18 s per scan and ~2.5 GB peak GPU memory. Predicted tumor burden tracks the reference across four orders of magnitude. Sub-millilitre lesions remain the main open problem.


> *Predicted and reference contours across kidney, liver, stomach, pancreas and extra-organ lesions, with per-case DSC.*


Full paper coming out soon. Joint work with Luca Pegolotti, Virginia Tasso, and Marco Santambrogio.


## Dinner with Nucleo at RSNA


If you are coming to RSNA, we would love to meet you. We are hosting a dinner in Chicago on Monday, 30 November, for radiologists and clinical teams working on body composition. It is one table, which keeps everyone in the same conversation and does mean seats are limited.


[Request a seat](https://luma.com/vg14eube)
